title: Document and gate the dangling provenance left by the 2026-09-10 repo recreation
description: Every @opum-ai/lore* version published before 0.6.1 carries SLSA provenance pinning a commit the 2026-09-10 repo delete/recreate destroyed. 0.6.0's attestation resolves to gitCommit 59ba30e497f8e98aa6c6be022d9363fd718fb4ee at refs/tags/v0.6.0; GitHub answers 422 'No commit found for SHA' for it, and its build run 34393976910 is 404. On npmjs.com this surfaces as a provenance link that cannot find the commit, which reads as tampering to anyone who does not know the history was rebuilt. The SHA still resolves in local clones' loose objects, so a git cat-file check wrongly says it is fine. Nothing repairs the existing links short of republishing. quest-cli confirmed the identical shape across all 8 of its pre-0.6.1 versions and already shipped the documented-not-repaired response in QCLI-267: a GitHub Release plus a --pre/--post provenance gate in release.yml. lore-cli has no equivalent. Filed 2026-09-13 out of the 0.6.1 release investigation; deliberately kept OUT of that release.

acceptanceCriteria.text: release-publishing.md carries a section explaining that pre-0.6.1 provenance links are permanently dangling, names the 2026-09-10 recreation as the cause, and states plainly that this is expected rather than tampering
The doc warns that the destroyed SHAs still resolve in local clones loose objects, so git cat-file is not a valid check -- the live GitHub API is
release.yml carries a provenance gate comparable to quest-cli QCLI-267s --pre/--post check, so a future history rewrite is caught at release time rather than discovered on npmjs.com
A GitHub Release exists for the affected tags, or the decision not to create one is recorded with its reasoning

comments.body:
SOURCE TEXT TO ADAPT, and one way it does NOT transfer.

quest-cli shipped the equivalent section on 2026-09-13: quest-cli PR #42, file
docs/runbooks/quest-cli-package-and-release.md, section "## A 404 on an old gitHead is
expected, not tampering" (commit be0c21e; not on their dev yet at this writing, so read it
from that commit, not from a checkout). They explicitly offered it for adaptation and said
nothing in it is quest-cli-specific except package and repo names.

THAT LAST PART IS NOT QUITE TRUE FOR US, and it is the reason this note exists. Their
section is framed end to end around npm's `gitHead` field. lore-cli's published versions do
not have one -- checked every version of @opum-ai/lore-darwin-arm64 on the registry, and
`gitHead` is absent from all of them, including 0.3.0, 0.5.0 and 0.6.0. Adapting their
prose by swapping names would produce a section telling readers to check a field that does
not exist on our packages, and a reader who checked and found nothing would reasonably
conclude the warning was stale.

lore-cli's dangling reference lives on a DIFFERENT surface: the SLSA provenance
attestation, not the packument. Retrieve it as

  curl -s "https://registry.npmjs.org/-/npm/v1/attestations/@opum-ai%2flore-darwin-arm64@0.6.0"

then base64-decode the sigstore bundle's dsseEnvelope.payload and read
predicate.buildDefinition.resolvedDependencies[0].digest.gitCommit, alongside
externalParameters.workflow.ref. For 0.6.0 that is gitCommit
59ba30e497f8e98aa6c6be022d9363fd718fb4ee at refs/tags/v0.6.0, and
`gh api repos/opum-ai/lore-cli/commits/59ba30e4...` answers 422. The build run named in
predicate.runDetails.metadata.invocationId (34393976910) is 404 for the same reason.

WHAT DOES TRANSFER VERBATIM: their "check this from the live GitHub API, never from a local
clone" paragraph, including the git cat-file trap. That reasoning is identical for us and is
the single most valuable line in the section -- keep it.

ALSO WORTH COPYING: their framing that this is a documentation entry and not a task because
the cure is worse than the condition (npm forbids republishing a version; re-pointing a tag
would still disagree with the immutable published metadata; the tarballs, checksums and
signatures are all intact and correctly signed -- only the commit the provenance names has
stopped existing). AC#4 on this task should almost certainly resolve as "decision not to
create a GitHub Release, recorded with reasoning" on the same grounds.

FOR AC#3, their forward gate is scripts/release-provenance.mjs wired into release.yml as
--pre/--post (QCLI-267). lore-cli has no equivalent. Build ours against the attestation
surface described above rather than gitHead, or it will check a field we never publish.
